name: Variegated Creeping Fig
description: Ficus pumila 'Variegata' is a variegated cultivar of the creeping fig (climbing fig), an evergreen woody vine in the Moraceae family native to East Asia (southern China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam). Juvenile foliage is small, heart-shaped to oval, with cream to white margins on light green leaves; variegation needs brighter light or it may revert to solid green. Like the species, it climbs or creeps via adhesive aerial roots and is popular for terrarium walls, backgrounds, and hanging baskets. Prefer bright indirect light, evenly moist but well-drained soil, and moderate to high humidity. Keep warm (about 15–27 °C); avoid drying out or waterlogging. Sap can irritate skin and the plant is toxic if ingested. Propagate from stem cuttings.
careTips: Provide bright indirect light to keep cream variegation; low light may cause reversion to green
Avoid harsh midday sun, which can scorch the delicate variegated leaves
Keep soil evenly moist; water when the top ~1 cm dries—never let roots dry out completely or sit in water
Use a well-draining, moisture-retentive mix; humidity helps buffer watering mistakes
Appreciates humidity above ~50%; mist or group plants if air is dry from AC/heat
Keep roughly 15–27 °C; variegated forms dislike cool winters below about 10 °C
Provide a wall, background, or support for climbing; prune to control spread
Propagate from stem cuttings with at least two leaves
Toxic if ingested; sap may irritate skin—keep away from pets and children
geographicOrigin: Cultivar of East Asian Ficus pumila (China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam)
